title: src/cli/internal/open.zig:155 uses macOS-shaped sigaction (breaks musl)
description:
`src/cli/internal/open.zig:155` writes
  sa.__sigaction_u.__sa_handler = sigterm_handler;
which is the macOS / BSD sigaction struct shape (signal handler nested
inside the `__sigaction_u` anonymous union). On Linux musl the field is
named differently (typically a top-level `handler` / `sa_handler`
field), so `-Dtarget=x86_64-linux-musl` fails to compile with:
  error: no field named '__sigaction_u' in struct 'cimport.struct_sigaction'

Surfaced when cross-targeting musl (e.g. on CI containers whose system
glibc-crt trips Zig 0.16's LLD on .sframe relocations and where musl
is the workaround target).

Acceptance criteria:
- `mise exec zig@0.16.0 -- zig build -Dtarget=x86_64-linux-musl` builds
  cleanly through `compile exe jelly`.
- `mise exec zig@0.16.0 -- zig build -Dtarget=x86_64-linux-musl smoke`
  passes (all CLI smoke steps green).
- The fix uses a portable struct-shape selector (e.g., `@hasField` or
  builtin.target.abi check) so both glibc-native and musl-native
  builds compile.
- No regression on the user's normal glibc-native build.

References:
- HEAD at fix time: 7c119f0 (post-show-fix)
- Originating note: PR #1 body under "Build / toolchain note"
close_reason: fixed by std.posix.Sigaction migration in src/cli/internal/open.zig:154-159 + sigterm_handler param: c_int → std.posix.SIG. Verified zig build -Dtarget=x86_64-linux-musl test (RAW_EXIT=0) and smoke (all 17 original CLI steps green; only failure is the unrelated pre-existing palace-mint missing-libvector.lbug_extension).

title: palace mint bridge fails when libvector.lbug_extension missing (smoke regression)
description:
## Root cause (revised after investigation 2026-06-02)

`@ladybugdb/core@0.15.3` ships `lbugjs.node` (the Node.js native
binding) but does NOT bundle vector-extension binaries. The vector
extension is downloaded on-demand by `INSTALL VECTOR` SQL into a
runtime cache at `~/.lbdb/extension/<lbdb_version>/<platform>/vector/`.

On this fleet container:
- npm pin: `@ladybugdb/core@^0.15.3` (package.json + bun.lock)
- Runtime cache present: `~/.lbdb/extension/0.15.0/linux_amd64/vector/libvector.lbug_extension`
  (1,028,296 bytes, dated 2026-05-24 — stale from a prior LadybugDB install)
- Required cache: `~/.lbdb/extension/0.15.3/linux_amd64/vector/libvector.lbug_extension` — ABSENT
- Failure mode: the 0.15.0 file's C++ ABI (`_ZTIN4lbug7catalog12IndexAuxInfoE`
  typeinfo symbol) does not match the 0.15.3 runtime, so loading it
  throws `undefined symbol`. On a clean container with no cache at
  all, `INSTALL VECTOR` would need to hit LadybugDB's extension CDN
  over the network — which fleet/CI may not have.

This isn't "missing extension" — it's "stale cache + ABI mismatch +
no clean-room fallback when offline".

## Concrete vendoring plan (bundle approach, no auto-fetch)

### 1. Lock the LadybugDB version

- `package.json`: tighten `"@ladybugdb/core": "^0.15.3"` → `"0.15.3"`
  (drop the caret) so the runtime version matches the vendored
  extension exactly.
- Bump discipline: any LadybugDB bump becomes a coordinated commit
  with refreshed `vendor/lbdb-vector/` bytes.

### 2. Vendor the extension binaries per platform

Layout under a new dir:
  vendor/lbdb-vector/0.15.3/linux_amd64/vector/libvector.lbug_extension
  vendor/lbdb-vector/0.15.3/linux_arm64/vector/libvector.lbug_extension
  vendor/lbdb-vector/0.15.3/darwin_arm64/vector/libvector.lbug_extension
  vendor/lbdb-vector/0.15.3/darwin_amd64/vector/libvector.lbug_extension (optional)
  vendor/lbdb-vector/0.15.3/win32_amd64/vector/libvector.lbug_extension (optional)

Per-platform size: ~1 MB based on the 0.15.0 file. Four platforms ≈
4 MB total — well under git-LFS thresholds; plain git is fine.

Bytes are obtained once by:
  (a) clean-room install on a network-enabled machine, run `INSTALL
      VECTOR` against `@ladybugdb/core@0.15.3`, copy
      `~/.lbdb/extension/0.15.3/<platform>/vector/libvector.lbug_extension`
      into the vendor tree; OR
  (b) direct download from LadybugDB's published extension URL
      (record the URL + SHA256 in vendor/lbdb-vector/README.md).

### 3. Wire the runtime to find the vendored bytes

Two options; investigate which LadybugDB 0.15.3 actually supports:

- **Option A — preflight populate `~/.lbdb/extension/`**: a
  `scripts/prepare-lbdb-extensions.ts` invoked from `package.json`
  `postinstall` (and explicitly from `scripts/cli-smoke.sh` and
  `scripts/server-smoke.sh` before they touch the palace) that
  copies `vendor/lbdb-vector/0.15.3/<host-platform>/vector/...`
  into `~/.lbdb/extension/0.15.3/<host-platform>/vector/...` if
  the target is missing or doesn't match the vendored SHA. This
  works regardless of any LadybugDB env knob.
- **Option B — env-var override**: if LadybugDB exposes a
  `LBDB_EXTENSION_DIR` (or equivalent) that overrides the default
  `~/.lbdb/extension/` lookup, point it at `vendor/lbdb-vector/0.15.3/`
  at process startup. Lighter touch, no file copy, no $HOME pollution.
  TBD whether 0.15.3 actually exposes this — needs source inspection.

Default to Option A as the safe path; switch to B if LadybugDB
supports the env-var hook.

### 4. Version-drift assertion

`scripts/check-lbdb-version.ts`:
- Reads `@ladybugdb/core` version from `node_modules/@ladybugdb/core/package.json`.
- Asserts a directory matching that version exists under `vendor/lbdb-vector/`.
- Fails CI loudly when the npm pin moves but the vendor tree wasn't refreshed.

Hook into `bun run check` (svelte-check is already there) or `bun
run test:unit` as a precondition.

### 5. Documentation

- `vendor/lbdb-vector/README.md`: how the bytes were obtained,
  download URLs, SHA256 per file, and the "how to refresh" recipe
  when bumping LadybugDB.
- New ADR `docs/decisions/2026-06-NN-vendored-lbdb-vector.md`
  explaining: why on-demand `INSTALL VECTOR` is rejected (network
  dependency + ABI fragility), why bundling beats auto-fetch
  (hermetic, deterministic, smaller-blast-radius), and the upkeep
  contract (version pin + refresh-on-bump).

## Acceptance criteria (replaces previous)

1. `vendor/lbdb-vector/0.15.3/` contains at least linux_amd64 and
   darwin_arm64 vector extension binaries (linux_arm64 too once
   verified).
2. `scripts/prepare-lbdb-extensions.ts` exists and is wired into
   `package.json` `postinstall` and the two smoke scripts.
3. `scripts/check-lbdb-version.ts` exists and runs as part of `bun
   run check` (or its own gate); it fails when versions drift.
4. `package.json` pins `@ladybugdb/core` to an exact version (no
   caret).
5. `zig build smoke` succeeds end-to-end on a clean container with
   no `~/.lbdb/` directory beforehand — including the palace-mint
   bridge step.
6. The new ADR exists and is dated.
7. `vendor/lbdb-vector/README.md` records the bytes' provenance
   (URL + SHA256 per file) and the refresh recipe.

## Open questions

- Does LadybugDB 0.15.3 expose an `LBDB_EXTENSION_DIR` env var (or
  equivalent native-binding config) that bypasses `~/.lbdb/extension/`?
  If yes → Option B is cleaner. Source inspection of
  `node_modules/@ladybugdb/core/lbug.d.ts` and the `INSTALL VECTOR`
  C++ path would settle this.
- Win32 + darwin_amd64 platforms — vendor only if we actually
  support them (i.e. if anyone runs smoke there).

Triggering INSTALL VECTOR with @ladybugdb/core@0.15.3 (native core internally 0.15.0) downloads a binary that still fails LOAD EXTENSION VECTOR with the same _ZTIN4lbug7catalog12IndexAuxInfoE symbol error. Upstream packaging mismatch: extension CDN is built against a newer host ABI than what npm @0.15.3 ships. Three options under consideration: (a) downgrade/upgrade lbug pin to find a known-good combo; (b) make INSTALL VECTOR lazy in store.server.ts so palace-mint smoke without vector ops passes; (c) build vector ext from source against the pinned host. Awaiting decision before resuming.

Tested @ladybugdb/core@{0.15.0,0.15.3,0.16.0,0.17.1} — every version downloads a vector extension that fails LOAD with the same _ZTIN4lbug7catalog12IndexAuxInfoE symbol (lbug::catalog::IndexAuxInfo typeinfo). title: Default Linux build to Zig-bundled musl for hermetic builds
description:
GCC 16's `crt1.o` started emitting `.sframe` unwind sections with
`R_X86_64_PC64` relocations that Zig 0.16's LLD cannot resolve.
This means `zig build` on any system with GCC 16+ glibc fails to link
the jelly exe (and tests) until either Zig adds support for those
relocations or the user passes `-Dtarget=x86_64-linux-musl` to use
Zig's bundled hermetic libc + crt.

Making musl the default on Linux:
- Removes the system libc/crt dependency entirely — "just zig and bun"
  becomes literally true.
- Sidesteps the GCC-16-vs-Zig-0.16-LLD toolchain skew permanently.
- Produces statically-linked binaries that run on any Linux box.
- Trade-off: ~200KB larger binary, marginal perf delta on some libc
  hot paths. Negligible for a CLI tool.

Acceptance criteria:
- `build.zig` defaults `target` to `x86_64-linux-musl` on Linux hosts
  (preserve native default on darwin and any other tag); `-Dtarget=...`
  still overrides.
- Bare `zig build` on any Linux host (including ones with new GCC)
  links successfully.
- ADR added under `docs/decisions/` dated today, explaining the trade-
  off and the toolchain history.
- All gates green under the new default: `zig build test`,
  `zig build smoke`, `scripts/cli-smoke.sh`.
- Depends on: open.zig sigaction fix (issue above) — without that,
  musl builds fail downstream of build.zig anyway.

References:
- PR #1 body under "Build / toolchain note"
close_reason: Bare zig build now produces statically-linked musl binary on Linux. build.zig:3-18 synthesises default_target via builtin.target.os.tag. -Dtarget=native opt-out preserved. ADR at docs/decisions/2026-05-24-hermetic-musl-default-linux.md. CLAUDE.md updated. zig build test exit 0; zig build smoke runs all 19 original CLI steps green (palace-mint bridge fails on pre-existing missing libvector.lbug_extension — environmental, not regression). PR #1 show-fix E2E still works under new default.

title: Extend musl default to aarch64-linux (currently hardcodes x86_64)
description:
Follow-up to Dreamball-3a1 (commit 8099201). The musl default in build.zig hardcodes `x86_64`:

  const default_target: std.Target.Query = if (@import("builtin").os.tag == .linux)
      .{ .cpu_arch = .x86_64, .os_tag = .linux, .abi = .musl }
  else
      .{};

An aarch64 Linux contributor running bare `zig build` gets an x86_64
musl binary cross-compiled, not a native aarch64 one. They'd need to
pass `-Dtarget=aarch64-linux-musl` (or `-Dtarget=native`) explicitly.

Acceptance criteria:
- build.zig synthesises `default_target` from `@import("builtin").target`
  on Linux so bare `zig build` produces a native-arch musl binary on
  both x86_64 and aarch64 hosts.
- macOS / other OS targets stay unchanged.
- `-Dtarget=native` and `-Dtarget=<explicit>` still override.
- `zig build && file zig-out/bin/jelly` reports the correct host arch
  (verified on at least an x86_64 host; aarch64 host verification is
  a separate ad-hoc test).
- The ADR at docs/decisions/2026-05-24-hermetic-musl-default-linux.md
  is updated with a one-line note about the arch-aware default.

Flagged by architect review during the post-PR-1 Ralph session.

References:
- Original musl default: commit 8099201
- Decision doc: docs/decisions/2026-05-24-hermetic-musl-default-linux.md
- Closes the aarch64 gap noted in the Ralph architect verification.
close_reason: build.zig now derives cpu_arch from builtin.target so bare zig build produces a native-arch musl binary on x86_64 and aarch64 Linux hosts. ADR's code snippet updated to match. Verified on this x86_64 container: zig build → statically-linked x86_64 ELF.
